title: Assad government collapses in Syria, putting Russia's Tartus and Hmeimim bases in question
body:
Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty reported on 9 December 2024 that the government of Syrian President Bashar al-Assad had fallen over the preceding weekend, placing in doubt the future of Russia's two military bases in Syria. Syria had granted Russia a 49-year lease covering access to the naval facility at Tartus and the Hmeimim air base. Tartus, on the Mediterranean coast, could moor up to 11 vessels, including nuclear-powered ships. Hmeimim lies about 60 kilometres up the coast.

Russia's intervention in Syria began in September 2015. At its peak around 2017, roughly 6,000 combat and auxiliary troops were deployed, and from September 2015 to January 2018 Russian forces flew more than 34,000 combat sorties, according to the Center for Strategic and International Studies.

As of 9 December there were no confirmed signs of a pullout. An unnamed Kremlin official told the TASS agency that Russia had reached an agreement to ensure the safety of its military assets in Syria, while Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said it was premature to discuss the matter. Satellite images showed Il-76 cargo aircraft parked at Hmeimim, which might indicate the start of an evacuation. The article attributed Assad's rapid collapse largely to the lack of support from Russia and Iran, noting that Russia's war in Ukraine limited its spare capacity.
